topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, its multidisciplinary audience, and the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and tissue basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal tissue architecture and differentiation programs, as well as the experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Characterization, progression, and nomenclature of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the pathological distinctions, progression stages, metastatic pathways, and standard naming systems for benign and malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physical, metabolic, and systemic mechanisms through which primary tumors and distant metastases cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor frequency and cancer mortality across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the rationale, histological basis, and diagnostic efficacy of population screening methods across various organ sites.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture with a concluding review of learning objectives and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
